mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 7% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 7% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the effect is absent during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and lowers profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during periods of falling energy prices.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and core consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening of monetary and inflationary pressures, which increases real discount rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the effect is absent when GDP growth is above 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated surge in both real personal income (implied by PAYEMS growth) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 6-month moving averages signals a robust demand recovery, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both exceed 6-month MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months, or the effect reverses during periods of rising unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the labor force participation rate (implied by stable UNRATE but rising PAYEMS) above its 12-month average for three consecutive months signals improved labor market dynamism, which expands consumer demand and corporate capacity, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE stable and PAYEMS > 12-month MA for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real retail sales (implied by RSAFS growth) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which lifts corporate revenues and profit margins, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.8%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during periods of aggressive monetary tightening.
